miniProject.title: An optimizer and numerics test bench
miniProject.brief: Build gradient descent, heavy-ball and AdamW with clipping, schedules and restartable state, a KKT and proximal-gradient pair checked against a solver, and stable reductions. Compare the optimizers on changed geometry against eigenvalue predictions, then diagnose one divergence and one finite-precision failure.
steps: Implement gradient descent, heavy-ball and AdamW with norm clipping, an update-indexed schedule and a state object holding parameters, moments, step count and schedule clock. Exit every loop with a status of converged, stagnated, non-finite or iteration cap, and force each status in tests.

Run all three on ill-conditioned quadratics, once diagonal and once rotated, predicting the gradient-descent rate from the eigenvalues first. Report the gradient norm and objective gap against gradient evaluations and compare with the prediction.

Diagnose one divergence past the stability limit by projecting iterates onto the eigenvectors and showing only the top mode growing at the predicted factor. Then add minibatch noise to finite-sum least squares and check the gradient covariance and the constant-step plateau against their formulas.

Check the AdamW moments against their finite geometric sums on a constant gradient. Then match `torch.optim.AdamW` on one deterministic quadratic under the same clipped gradients and per-step rates, save and resume mid-run, and use the unclipped full gradient as the stationarity residual.

Solve a changed two-coordinate QP by hand and with CVXPY and Clarabel, recording every KKT residual with solver status. Derive soft thresholding, then check a lasso proximal loop against a closed form on a diagonal case and against a solver residual on the general case.

Build log-sum-exp, left-to-right, balanced and Kahan sums, and online mean and variance, testing cancellation, large offsets and low-precision storage with higher-precision accumulation against `math.fsum` and higher-precision oracles. Diagnose one finite-precision failure end to end and show the repair.
deliverables: `numlab/optim/`: optimizers with exit statuses and restartable state, KKT and proximal code, and the reductions.
Tests for rate predictions, the divergence projection, noise checks, the AdamW oracle and resume, KKT residuals, lasso checks and reduction oracles.
`notes/optimization.md` with predictions beside measurements and both failure diagnoses.

rubric.pass: Measured gradient-descent rates on diagonal and rotated quadratics are compared with eigenvalue predictions.
rubric.strong: Rotation is shown not to change the gradient-descent rate, with the reason, and momentum gains are reported per gradient evaluation.

rubric.pass: The divergent run is traced to the top eigenmode at the predicted factor, and noise covariance and plateau match their formulas.
rubric.strong: Exit statuses separate divergent, stagnated and converged runs without manual inspection.

rubric.pass: AdamW matches PyTorch within a stated tolerance and resume equals the uninterrupted run.
rubric.strong: A test shows restoring parameters without moments or the schedule clock changes the trajectory.

rubric.pass: The QP records every KKT residual with solver status, and the lasso passes its optimality residual.
rubric.strong: Residuals carry stated tolerances, and solver success is never accepted without them.

rubric.pass: Each reduction matches its oracle, and one finite-precision failure is diagnosed and repaired.
rubric.strong: The note separates precision lost in storage from precision lost in accumulation.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone optimizer stability: the optimizer comparison, the divergence diagnosis and the finite-precision failure.
